title: fix(ci): never let bots trigger the Polli auto-fix agent
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes the `pollinations-ai[bot]` ID from the auto-fix allowlist; any `Bot` sender now has the `POLLI` label removed without a comment
- Triage workflow no longer applies the `POLLI` label from the LLM verdict; it comments that a maintainer can hand small fixes to Polli
- Closes the chain: untrusted issue text → LLM verdict → bot-applied label → write-capable `claude-code-action`

Reported by @fisventurous in Discord (repo safety review); confirmed against `main`.

Remaining findings from the same review are not in this PR: sender gate on `apps-publish-submissions.yml`, SDK/UI/MCP tests in PR CI, filename interpolation in CI shell steps.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: Polli gets a human gate
gist.blurb: Polli’s auto-fix garden now has a proper gatekeeper. Bots can no longer pass each other a label and accidentally summon a write-capable helper.
gist.summary: Updated the issue triage and Polli auto-fix workflows so any Bot sender has its POLLI label silently removed, while LLM triage verdicts now leave a maintainer-facing handoff comment instead of applying the label.
gist.impact: Maintainers retain an explicit human handoff before Polli’s write-capable auto-fix action runs, closing the bot-label chain from untrusted issue text to repository changes.

A glowing retro terminal and code-plants show the protected automation behind the gate.
